newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - April 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - April 25.

text.p: The New York Times reports the following stories on its front page on Friday:
* Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott announced his support of the Chemical Weapons Convention and the Senate moved towards approving the pact.
* The U.S. Justice Department said it would not try to block the $22 billion merger between NYNEX and Bell Atlantic.
* A specutacular site of dinosaur fossils was discovered in a remote region in northeast China, an international team of paleontologists announced.
* To gain support for the Chemical Weapons Convention, the Clinton Administration tried to mobilise many of the older Republican leaders who had negotiated the pact.
* European scientist Luc Montagnier, co-discoverer of the AIDS virus, said he would move much of his research base from Paris to Queens College, part of City University of New York.

* The trial began in the Oklahoma City bombing case, with the government opening its case against Timothy McVeigh by painting him as a right-wing extremist who wanted to use violence to cause a second American Revolution.

* The Peruvian government said the bodies of the 14 guerrillas killed in Tuesday's successful hostage rescue would be buried in unmarked graves, amid allegations that some rebels were killed as they tried to surrender.
